shortDescription: Swedish utility Vattenfall reported on Thursday a fall in third-quarter underlying profit despite higher electricity prices due to the war in the Middle East, as nuclear power outages and lower hydrological balance weighed.($1 = 9.8939 Swedish crowns)

children: Swedish utility Vattenfall reported on Thursday a fall in third-quarter underlying profit despite higher electricity prices due to the war in the Middle East, as nuclear power outages and lower hydrological balance weighed.
Underlying operating profit at the state-owned group fell 38% from a year earlier to 3.81 billion crowns ($385 million) on a 13% sales drop

Vattenfall said lower volumes from nuclear power mainly due to outages of the Ringhals 3 and 4 nuclear reactors, as well as lower hydro power volumes due to weaker hydrological balance, weighed on profits
Average day-ahead prices in the Nordic region increased 107% to  €74.4 per megawatt hour (MWh) during the quarter, Vattenfall said
In Germany and the Netherlands, they were up 52% and 60%, respectively, Vattenfall said in a statement
The Middle East conflict has sent oil and gas prices surging

"It’s fair to anticipate that (European energy) prices will continue to be volatile throughout the winter," CFO Kerstin Ahlfont told Reuters. "Gas storage levels are lower than typical for this time of year ... and clearly there is concern regarding these levels."
